title: Electronic Health Record-Embedded Workflow to Operationalize Whole-Person Screening in Safety-Net Primary Care: Observational Implementation Evaluation Study.
abstract:
Background

Health systems increasingly screen patients for social and whole-person needs. Yet, electronic health record data often remain passive when no workflow translates identified needs into structured action during routine care. In safety-net and federally qualified health center (FQHC) settings, this gap is especially consequential because clinicians must address multidomain needs within time-constrained encounters while meeting documentation, coding, and referral requirements.

Objective

This study evaluated the implementation and recorded use of an Epic-based digital workflow that links a Whole PERSON Health Score (WPHS) assessment to a Best Practice Advisory (BPA) and SmartSet, along with a separate Power BI accountability dashboard, in a safety-net FQHC network.

Methods

We conducted an observational implementation evaluation of the WPHS BPA-SmartSet workflow at Riverside University Health System using the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance) framework. We analyzed encounter-level WPHS assessments and BPA presentation records from January 2023 through July 2026. We examined screening reach, temporal correspondence between BPA presentations and preceding qualifying WPHS assessments, recorded downstream workflow activity, variation across clinics, and trends over time using descriptive statistics. As a sensitivity analysis, we estimated logistic regression models with clinic fixed effects and 2-way patient- and provider-clustered robust SEs to evaluate temporal patterns in SmartSet opening and downstream workflow activity.

Results

During the study period, 177,821 WPHS assessments were completed among 115,022 unique patients; 173,763/177,821 (97.7%) identified at least one qualifying yellow or red domain. Among 107,010 BPA presentations involving 101,297 unique patients, 104,049 (97.2%) were linked to a uniquely identifiable most-recent qualifying WPHS assessment; among these, 99.1% (103,122/104,049) occurred within 7 days. The SmartSet was opened in 82.9% (88,736/107,010) of BPA presentations, and broad structured downstream workflow activity was documented in 82.4% (88,160/107,010); Z-code documentation in 42.6% (45,632/107,010), and referrals in 23.4% (25,061/107,010). SmartSet opening increased from 41.3% (262/634) in January 2023 to 94.3% (4262/4520) in July 2026.

Conclusions

In this safety-net FQHC setting, whole-person need was common and often multidomain, and an Epic BPA-SmartSet workflow was associated with high rates of SmartSet opening and documented downstream workflow activity across observed BPA presentations. BPA presentations were highly concordant with preceding qualifying WPHS assessments, and workflow activity increased substantially over the implementation period. For digital health leaders seeking to operationalize whole-person care, the findings support electronic health record-based decision support that surfaces identified need, bundles documentation and referral tasks, and pairs point-of-care workflow with visible implementation monitoring, rather than relying on screening alone.

title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

title: A Disease Trajectory Representation Framework With Risk-Aware Pseudotime Analysis for Electronic Health Records: Application to Heart Failure Risk Stratification.
abstract:
Background

Heart failure develops through complex longitudinal interactions among multiple chronic diseases, making longitudinal disease trajectories an important source of clinical information. Longitudinal disease trajectories contain rich structural information that reflects disease evolution and comorbidity interactions. However, this information is often lost when electronic health record (EHR) data are summarized using conventional pooling strategies or sparse International Classification of Diseases (ICD) representations.

Objective

This study aimed to develop an interpretable trajectory representation that preserves structural characteristics of longitudinal disease evolution for heart failure risk stratification using EHRs.

Methods

Longitudinal ICD trajectories were represented using Node2Vec embeddings and summarized with information gain (IG)-weighted geometric features, including historical means, directional shifts, dispersion, and deviation relative to high-risk disease representations. The resulting maximum IG-weighted deviation geometric (mIGwDG) representation was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation against conventional embedding aggregation strategies, sparse ICD one-hot encoding, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) model. To facilitate interpretation of longitudinal disease evolution, we further developed a risk-aware pseudotime framework to organize patient trajectories along a model-inferred risk continuum and used a framework combining IG with the positive pointwise mutual information (PPMI) framework to characterize clinically relevant comorbidity patterns.

Results

The proposed framework achieved an out-of-fold (OOF) area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.667 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888, outperforming conventional embedding aggregation methods. Compared with sparse ICD one-hot encoding, the proposed framework reduced feature dimensionality by approximately 75% while maintaining comparable predictive performance. Combining mIGwDG with sparse ICD one-hot features further improved both logistic regression (LR) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), suggesting that the proposed representation captures complementary longitudinal disease trajectory information. In addition, the risk-aware pseudotime framework organized heterogeneous patient trajectories along a model-inferred risk continuum, while IG×PPMI analysis highlighted clinically relevant comorbidity patterns that supported the interpretation of longitudinal disease organization.

Conclusions

The proposed framework provides a compact and interpretable representation of longitudinal disease trajectories while maintaining comparable predictive performance. By combining geometric trajectory characterization with risk-aware pseudotime visualization, the framework facilitates the representation of longitudinal EHRs, the visualization of disease evolution, and risk stratification.

title: Artificial intelligence for cerebrovascular digital subtraction angiography: methods, evidence, and challenges.
abstract: Cerebrovascular diseases remain a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) provides high-spatiotemporal-resolution visualization of cerebrovascular anatomy and contrast-agent dynamics and plays an important role in diagnosis, interventional treatment planning, and treatment assessment. Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly been applied to cerebrovascular DSA, yet the available evidence is distributed across diverse imaging settings, technical tasks, datasets, and validation strategies. This structured topical review provides a DSA-centered overview of AI-assisted cerebrovascular image analysis across 2D DSA, three-dimensional rotational angiography, and four-dimensional DSA. Literature from Web of Science Core Collection and major engineering databases was screened at title, abstract, and full-text levels using predefined eligibility criteria. The literature is organized around six interconnected tasks: image preprocessing, vessel and lesion segmentation, image registration, reconstruction and generation, disease diagnosis and detection, and hemodynamic analysis. Representative conventional and learning-based methods are reviewed together with their datasets, evaluation metrics, validation designs, and available data or code resources, with particular attention to the strength and limitations of the supporting evidence. Recent studies demonstrate increasing use of spatiotemporal modeling, deep learning, and image-generation techniques, but clinical translation remains constrained by small or single-center datasets, heterogeneous acquisition protocols and evaluation practices, limited external and prospective validation, model interpretability, and deployment requirements. Future work should emphasize acquisition-aware and physics-informed modeling, multicenter and privacy-preserving collaboration, clinically meaningful validation, and closer integration with neurointerventional workflows. By linking methodological developments with their supporting evidence and translational challenges, this review aims to support the development of more robust and clinically applicable AI methods for cerebrovascular DSA.

title: Viability of Public Statistics-Based Synthetic Personas in Small-Area Public Health Surveillance: Sociodemographic Benchmark Consistency Study Using Korea Community Health Survey and Korean Statistical Information Service Data.
abstract:
Background

Synthetic population and persona datasets can provide artificial individual-level records without exposing personal data. However, for surveillance use, they must preserve the joint profiles that define vulnerable groups, not only marginal distributions.

Objective

This study evaluated whether a public statistics-based Korean synthetic persona dataset is consistent with Korea Community Health Survey (CHS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) benchmarks for auxiliary small-area public health surveillance.

Methods

We compared 1,000,000 synthetic persona rows with 1,156,122 adult respondents from the 2021-2025 CHS and selected KOSIS municipal indicators. Core variables were age group, sex, marital status, living-alone status, and education; province or municipal area replaced marital status in the regional profiles. Economic activity and occupation were treated as sensitivity domains. We compared marginal and joint distributions using percentage-point differences and total variation distance (TVD) and quantified CHS sampling uncertainty using 500-replicate stratified cluster percentile bootstrap intervals and compared high-dimensional TVD with CHS split-half references. Sparse-cell, KOSIS correlation, and regional composition-standardized analyses assessed robustness and potential downstream use.

Results

Persona rows were close to CHS for sex (TVD<0.001, 95% bootstrap percentile interval 0.000-0.001), province (TVD 0.006, bootstrap percentile interval 0.005-0.006), living-alone status (TVD 0.008, bootstrap percentile interval 0.007-0.009), and age group (TVD 0.013, bootstrap percentile interval 0.012-0.014). Differences were larger for marital status (TVD 0.039, bootstrap percentile interval 0.038-0.040) and education (TVD 0.059, bootstrap percentile interval 0.058-0.061). The national core profile had a TVD of 0.106 (bootstrap percentile interval 0.105-0.107), compared with a CHS split-half median of 0.009 (2.5th-97.5th percentile 0.008-0.011). The municipal profile had an observed TVD of 0.117, a bootstrap mean of 0.122 (95% bootstrap percentile interval 0.120-0.123), and a split-half median of 0.082 (2.5th-97.5th percentile 0.080-0.084). After restriction to CHS cells with n≥100, the municipal TVD decreased to 0.091. At the municipal level, CHS- and persona-composition standardized unmet health care rates differed by a mean of 0.109 percentage points (Pearson r=0.567), but standardization with national profile-specific probabilities did not reproduce observed local CHS rates (Pearson r=0.004 for persona composition). The conditional KOSIS living-alone comparison was modest (Pearson r=0.547).

Conclusions

The synthetic persona data showed close agreement for several basic demographic margins but less consistent agreement for high-dimensional sociodemographic profiles. They may support composition-based scenario development and dashboard prototyping but should not be used as stand-alone sources for local surveillance or health-outcome inference without additional calibration and validation.

title: Unveiling the molecular and biological mechanisms of Tai Chi in chronic disease management: a bibliometric and visualized analysis.
abstract:
Tai Chi is widely utilized for chronic disease management, yet its underlying biological mechanisms remain fragmented. To objectively map the mechanistic knowledge structure and identify emerging frontiers, a bibliometric analysis was conducted on 348 mechanism-focused articles spanning from 2006 to 2026, retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Data visualization and network analyses using VOSviewer and CiteSpace revealed a clear paradigm shift from macroscopic systemic responses to highly specific neurobiological targets. Early foundational research centered on psychoneuroimmunology, demonstrating that Tai Chi buffers the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and downregulates pro-inflammatory cytokines, thereby alleviating osteoarthritis pain and cancer-related fatigue. Contemporary research frontiers are heavily concentrated on neuroplasticity and cellular defense. Objective evidence highlights the upregulation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and the remodeling of cortico-limbic networks to preserve function in Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment. Furthermore, strong recent keyword bursts for "oxidative stress" and "heart failure" underscore Tai Chi's potential in enhancing endogenous antioxidant defenses, reducing DNA damage, and improving endothelial function via systemic brain-body crosstalk. In conclusion, Tai Chi exerts its multidimensional clinical benefits through interconnected neuro-immune, neuroplastic, and anti-oxidative networks. To transition from associative findings to definitive causal mechanisms, future research must integrate multi-omics technologies and rigorously standardized longitudinal trials.

title: Prioritizing Human Factors in the Clinical Translation of Mixed Reality Surgical Guidance.
abstract: Mixed reality and augmented reality technologies are increasingly being explored for intraoperative visualization, navigation, and surgical decision support. However, translation into routine surgical practice will depend not only on technical accuracy but also on whether these systems are usable, physically tolerable, and robust in the operating room environment. In this Viewpoint, we highlight 3 human factors domains that warrant greater attention in mixed reality surgical guidance: physical characteristics, dexterity and motor demands, and environmental factors. Published work has repeatedly drawn attention to challenges, including ergonomic burden, limited field of view, headset weight, visual and perceptual constraints, fatigue, and interaction burdens associated with gesture and voice control. These issues are often compounded by environmental conditions, such as noise, glare, crowding, and occlusion in real clinical settings. Although mixed reality may improve spatial awareness and reduce attention shifts in some settings, these benefits remain constrained by persistent usability, workflow, and environmental limitations. Viewed through a broader systems human factors lens, discussion remains concentrated mainly on user-device interaction and selected task-level issues, with comparatively less attention to team, organizational, training, and governance factors. We argue that future human factors research should move beyond technical validation alone and adopt a broader systems perspective that addresses user diversity, sterile and low-burden interaction, environmental resilience, and the wider conditions required for safe clinical integration. Such an approach is essential if mixed reality surgical guidance systems are to become safe, usable, and clinically adoptable.

title: Advances in retinal cellular imaging: Towards single-cell resolution and functional biomarkers.
abstract: Retinal imaging has traditionally described tissue and layer level pathology, whereas direct assessment of individual cells in the living human retina has been limited by ocular aberrations, optical contrast and image analysis constraints. Adaptive optics (AO) has substantially changed this landscape by improving lateral resolution and enabling in vivo visualization of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), ganglion-cell-layer structures, immune cells and microvasculature. This review discusses human retinal cellular imaging across three major AO-enhanced platforms: flood-illumination adaptive optics (FIAO), adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) and adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO). These modalities provide complementary capabilities, including rapid en face imaging, depth-resolved volumetric assessment and flexible confocal, non-confocal and fluorescence-based contrast. Recent progress is also being shaped by faster wavefront correction, wider-field acquisition, compressed multichannel imaging, sensorless AO and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted reconstruction, segmentation and quantification. Beyond optical resolution, molecular labeling strategies are beginning to add biological specificity to retinal cellular imaging. Indocyanine green (ICG) supports AO-assisted assessment of RPE mosaic contrast, annexin V-based Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) provides a molecular readout of retinal cell stress and apoptosis, and curcumin-based imaging has been explored as an experimental retinal amyloid marker in Alzheimer's disease. Together, these advances indicate a shift from high-resolution visualization alone towards cellular and molecular biomarkers of disease activity, progression and treatment response. Further translation will require standardized acquisition, robust automated analysis, multimodal validation and larger prospective studies across devices, disease populations and clinical sites.

title: Global research trends on healthcare-associated infections in the context of natural disasters, epidemics and pandemics.
abstract: IntroductionHealthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a serious public health concern. HAIs risk increases extraordinary events such as natural disasters, epidemics, and pandemics.Material and MethodsThis study analyzes publication trends related to HAIs in these contexts using bibliometric methods. Publications on HAIs related to natural disasters, epidemics, and pandemics from Scopus without year or document type restrictions were analyzed using VOSviewer to assess trends, keyword co-occurrence, citations, and country productivity.ResultsA total of 774 publications were analyzed, including 749 on epidemics/pandemics, and 25 on natural disasters. Publications increased notably during epidemics/pandemics, especially during COVID-19. The USA and China were leading publishing countries. Keyword analysis showed that "covıd-19" and "SARS-CoV-2" were most frequent in epidemic-/pandemic-related research, while "earthquake" appeared commonly in disaster-related studies.Before 2015, "nosocomial infections" was widely used, later replaced by "healthcare-associated infections." From 2018, studies focused more on multidrug-resistant organisms like methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. Recent years emphasized ventilator-associated pneumonia, mechanical ventilation, and Clostridioides difficile infections. Limited keyword data prevented overlay visualization for natural disasters.ConclusionsResearch on HAIs intensifies during epidemiological crises but remains limited for natural disasters, highlighting the need for further interdisciplinary studies to better understand and reduce HAI risks.

title: Advancing cyber-physical systems in surgery through a smart cyber operating theater testbed for medical device integration and clinical translation.
abstract:
Purpose

Operating-room devices and robotic systems are often standalone, which limits synchronized multi-source data utilization and cyber-physical surgical support. This Short Communication presents an integration approach for a Smart Cyber Operating Theater (SCOT) based on OPeLiNK, and reports log-based operational reliability in a clinical SCOT environment. Our focus is the architecture and feasibility of time-synchronized data integration rather than clinical outcome evaluation.

Methods

OPeLiNK was implemented as a common interface and integration architecture consisting of device-specific providers, a data server for management and time synchronization, and application-level data distribution. A university SCOT testbed was established in 2016 for onboarding and integration verification without interrupting clinical workflow. Operational reliability was assessed using de-identified integration logs collected in the clinical SCOT environment (HyperSCOT), defining a successful session as meeting all criteria: required device connection, data reception, application-level display, and time synchronization.

Results

The SCOT testbed enabled integration across heterogeneous connections (e.g., Ethernet, serial communication, USB, and video outputs) and supported verification of interconnectivity, including communication validation, data structure consistency, and behavior under abnormal termination and restart. As an application example, a Surgical Strategy Desk was demonstrated using simulated/demo data to show synchronized multi-source visualization. In the clinical environment, SCOT has been used since 2019, including at least 437 glioma surgeries, providing real-world operational logs to support the log-based reliability assessment.

Conclusions

We present an OPeLiNK-based SCOT integration approach and a testbed framework for safe onboarding and verification, complemented by log-based operational evidence from clinical use since 2019. Although clinical effectiveness and efficiency outcomes are out of scope for this Short Communication, reliable time-synchronized integration is a necessary foundation for future cyber-physical operating theaters and advanced decision support applications.

title: Minimally Invasive vs. Open L5-S1 Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion (TLIF): A Retrospective Comparison of Fusion Outcomes.
abstract:
Study design

Single-center retrospective cohort study.

Objective

To compare fusion and perioperative and clinical outcomes between minimally invasive (MIS) and open transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) at L5-S1.

Summary of background data

MIS-TLIF reduces soft-tissue disruption, blood loss, and hospital stay compared with open TLIF, but may increase fluoroscopy use and limit visualization for endplate preparation; data isolating the biomechanically demanding L5-S1 level with rigorous fusion assessment are limited.

Methods

Adults undergoing single-level L5-S1 TLIF from 2018-2023 were stratified by approach (MIS vs. open). Inclusion required 12-month postoperative CT and/or flexion-extension radiographs for fusion assessment. Perioperative variables, complications, reoperations, and patient-reported outcomes were compared using χ2 or Fisher tests and t tests or Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.

Results

Fifty-six patients met criteria (23 MIS, 33 open) with similar baseline demographics. Fusion rates were 91% with MIS and 73% with open TLIF (P=0.168). MIS-TLIF had lower estimated blood loss (148 vs. 229 mL, P=0.075) and shorter length of stay (2.8 vs. 3.9 d, P=0.034), but higher fluoroscopy dose (36.8 vs. 34.0 mGy, P=0.006). Operative time, complication rates (13% vs. 36%, P=0.103), reoperation rates (17% vs. 15%, P=1.0), and 12-month categorical patient-reported back pain, leg pain, and quality-of-life outcomes were comparable between groups.

Conclusions

At L5-S1, MIS-TLIF achieves fusion and clinical outcomes comparable to open TLIF while reducing blood loss and hospital stay at the cost of increased radiation exposure. These findings suggest that MIS-TLIF may offer perioperative advantages while demonstrating comparable observed fusion and clinical outcomes relative to open TLIF at L5-S1.

title: Flexible Nasolaryngoscopy for Pulmonologists: Narrative Review.
abstract:
Background

Flexible nasolaryngoscopy (FNL) enables dynamic visualization of the upper and 'middle' airways. Traditionally performed by otolaryngologists, FNL is of increasing relevance to pulmonology. Integrating FNL into everyday pulmonology practice could provide critical, management-altering data, facilitate timely diagnosis and optimized management of complex clinical presentations.

Objective

To delineate the role, indications, and training needs for FNL in adult pulmonology, and to summarize existing models of competency development relevant to pulmonologists.

Methods

A narrative review was performed using MEDLINE from database inception to November 2025. Sources included specialty guidelines, educational reports, and competency frameworks, with the aim of synthesizing evidence for pulmonology-focused training integration.

Results

Several indications for FNL are relevant to pulmonologists in day-to-day practice including breathlessness, chronic cough, and hemoptysis. FNL enables point-of-care evaluation of upper/middle airway pathologies. Existing competency frameworks focus on simulation, structured supervision, and workplace-based assessments rather than procedural volume. Comparable principles can inform a pulmonology-led FNL curriculum using established bronchoscopy training infrastructure. Potential gaps include simulation access, credentialing structures, and validated performance metrics.

Conclusion

FNL represents a natural extension of pulmonology, enabling diagnostic precision, integrated airway care, and holistic, patient-centered holistic management. Development of structured, competency-based, multidisciplinary training and assessment pathways for FNL is essential to ensure safe, standardized practice in pulmonology.

title: Augmented reality paradigm and EA-DGCNN decoding algorithm for motor imagery in stroke patients.
abstract: Objective.Stroke represents one of the leading causes of long-term motor dysfunction on a global scale. Existing motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interface (BCI) rehabilitation training systems face critical challenges of suboptimal patient engagement and limited electroencephalography (EEG) feature decoding capacity. To overcome these challenges, this study presents two primary original contributions: an independently designed wearable augmented reality (AR) MI training paradigm and a novel Euclidean alignment-based Dynamic Graph Convolutional Neural Network (EA-DGCNN) end-to-end decoding architecture.Approach.The immersive AR-MI paradigm heightens patient engagement and enhances MI performance. The EA-DGCNN model incorporates Euclidean alignment to minimize inter-subject variability in EEG distributions. The model extracts multi-dimensional spatiotemporal features via convolutional block attention, dynamic graph attention, and multi-scale convolutions, incorporating a Broad Learning System to achieve precise classification results.Main results.Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves an accuracy of 85.13 ± 10.53% on the public BCI Competition IV 2a dataset. On a custom clinical dataset of 20 stroke patients, the AR paradigm yields a classification accuracy of 71.9 ± 8.9%, outperforming the 68.9 ± 8.0% of the traditional 2D paradigm. Furthermore, evaluations on the 64-channel PhysioNet benchmark demonstrate robust cross-subject transferability with a superior grand-average accuracy of 83.67 ± 8.52%. Neurophysiological feature analysis indicates that the AR paradigm elicits more pronounced event-related desynchronization and event-related synchronization responses. The t-SNE visualization demonstrates that the AR paradigm, coupled with the proposed model, produces highly discriminative feature clustering patterns.Significance.This study delivers a more effective paradigm and a robust decoding solution for clinical BCI rehabilitation.

title: CASSFormer: A Lightweight CNN-Transformer Hybrid Network for Real-Time Coronary Artery Stenosis Detection and Localization.
abstract: Coronary angiography (CAG) is the clinical gold standard for assessing coronary artery stenosis. However, its two-dimensional projection nature often causes vessel overlap and limited contrast, making subtle or complex stenotic regions difficult to detect and localize, thereby increasing reliance on experienced cardiologists. Existing deep learning methods face a practical trade-off: CNN-based models struggle with low-contrast or small-scale lesions, while Transformer-based models incur high computational cost, limiting real-time applicability. To address these challenges, we propose Coronary Angiography Structure-aware Stenosis Transformer (CASSFormer), a lightweight CNN-Transformer hybrid network for real-time coronary artery stenosis detection and localization. Specifically, CASSFormer integrates three key components: (i) a multi-stage spatial feature downsampling module (MSFD) to preserve fine-grained vascular textures during early feature extraction; (ii) a multi-scale mixed-topology block (MMTB) to model elongated vessel structures and multi-scale stenotic patterns; (iii) a dual-attention cross-scale adaptive fusion module (DCAF) that jointly exploits local directional attention and global channel attention to enhance sensitivity to low-contrast and small-scale stenotic regions. Experiments on a large private clinical dataset and two public datasets (ARCADE, ADSD) show that CASSFormer achieves favorable detection and localization performance compared with mainstream detection models, while maintaining low computational overhead (27.1 GFLOPs, 11.9M parameters) and an average inference time of 8.0 ms per image. Visualization results further suggest its robustness under challenging angiographic conditions, including vessel overlap, distal small vessels, and severe stenosis or vessel interruption associated with myocardial infarction. These results support CASSFormer as an efficient assistive tool for stenosis detection and localization in complex CAG scenarios.

title: Primary Care Practice Productivity and Efficiency: Qualitative Evaluation of a Novel Clinic-Based Measure.
abstract:
Background

Existing primary care productivity and efficiency measures focus on the quantity of care delivered, without accounting for interprofessional teamwork invested or quality of care produced. We previously developed a novel productivity measure called Interprofessional Technical Efficiency Measure (ITEM) and tested it quantitatively across Veterans Affairs (VA) primary care practices. ITEM measures primary care practice efficiency in producing four primary care output measures (access, clinical quality of care, patient care experiences, and number of patients served) given staff time invested (inputs), while accounting for patient population complexity.

Objective

To qualitatively assess ITEM's validity and potential usefulness through feedback from VA primary care directors, data experts, and frontline clinical team leaders.

Design

We used rapid qualitative analysis of data from semi-structured interviews and focus groups to assess feedback on ITEM results.

Participants

A convenience sample of 34 interprofessional primary care leaders, managers, and frontline clinical team members from nine geographically dispersed VA medical centers and affiliated community-based outpatient clinics (CBOCs).

Approach

Participants reviewed graphic data visualizations comparing their scores to national VA averages. Qualitative thematic analysis focused on face, construct, and content validity, and usefulness for primary care efficiency improvement.

Results

Overall, participants perceived the ITEM measure as having face, construct, and content validity, and viewed ITEM and its data visualization approach as potentially useful for primary care practice efficiency improvement. Participant concerns focused on lack of measures of team functioning or burnout, data time lags related to practice team composition or output changes, potential alternative measures of ITEM outputs, and potential additional local context measures.

Conclusions

Primary care leaders and clinicians were receptive to a new productivity and efficiency measure that integrated quality and quantity of care goals, and to ITEM as a promising approach. Findings support continued ITEM development for use in primary care practice efficiency improvement initiatives.

title: How high sensitivity cardiac Troponin Point of Care Testing can be integrated into existing or new pathways for chest pain assessment in the emergency department.
abstract: Chest pain is a leading cause of Emergency Department (ED) admissions, accounting for about 10% of cases in Italy. Rapid detection of ischemic events using high-sensitivity cardiac Troponin I (hs-cTnI) enables faster rule-out and improved patient flow. However, turn-around time (TAT) may be delayed by sample transport and centralized lab processing. This study aims to assess the time and economic advantages of implementing Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) for hs-cTnI in the ED. Our observational study included 86 adults with atraumatic chest pain consecutively presenting to the ED (September-October 2024). Hs-cTnI was measured at triage using a POCT device and in the Central Laboratory. Time to result availability, ED length of stay, and operating costs were extracted from hospital systems. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, and POCT versus laboratory turnaround times were compared using the Mann-Whitney test. A statistically significant difference between central laboratory and POCT (median 80 vs 4.5) mean time between blood collection and visualization of hs-cTnI results by the ED physician was found. Even though the POCT cost per test is higher than the central laboratory, the use of POCT may help saving about €25 per patient by reducing ED length of stay (LOS). In conclusion, POCT hs-cTnI testing at triage significantly shortens time to clinical decision-making in chest pain patients, reducing ED length of stay and helping mitigate overcrowding. Despite higher analytical costs, the time saved yields an overall economic benefit, supporting POCT adoption for early risk stratification in the ED.

title: Total-Body <sup>18</sup>F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis assessment; however, its invasiveness limits its suitability for routine clinical use. The rising prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma underscores the need for reliable noninvasive assessment. Current noninvasive imaging methods provide surrogate measures of fibrosis but do not directly assess fibrogenic activity. In contrast, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables molecular imaging of activated fibroblasts, a key driver of fibrosis. This study evaluates dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET imaging to assess hepatic fibrogenic activity in MASLD. Methods: In this prospective pilot study, 10 subjects (3 healthy volunteers, 4 patients with mild-moderate fibrosis, and 3 patients with advanced fibrosis) underwent 60-min dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET/CT. SUV and blood-normalized SUV ratio (SUVR) were quantified across time frames, and the net influx rate was derived from dynamic data. MR elastography-derived liver stiffness values were obtained for comparison. Correlations with histologic fibrosis scoring of biopsy tissue were assessed using Spearman analysis. Results: At 5 min postinjection, SUVR correlated strongly with histologic fibrosis score (ρ = 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.00; P = 1.89 × 10-5), followed by SUV (ρ = 0.78; 95% CI, 0.23-0.98; P = 0.0077) and net influx rate from kinetic modeling (ρ = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.41-0.98; P = 0.0022). SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval allowed clearer differentiation among healthy volunteers, patients with mild fibrosis, and patients with advanced fibrosis. Conclusion: Dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.

title: Effects of non-pharmacological interventions on older adults with cognitive impairment in nursing homes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
Background

Older adults living with cognitive impairment in nursing homes experience multiple, co-occurring challenges across cognitive, physical, psychological, and social domains. However, it remains unclear which non-pharmacological interventions are most effective in addressing these multidimensional needs across different health domains. This network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to compare the effects of five categories of non-pharmacological interventions across five outcome domains and to identify the most effective strategies.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, VIP Chinese Science and Technology Periodical Database, and SinoMed for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating non-pharmacological interventions for older adults with cognitive impairment in nursing homes from database inception until November 2025. Two researchers independently screened the literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias. All analyses were conducted within a frequentist framework. Stata 14.0 (with the mvmeta and network packages) was used for primary network meta-analysis, intervention ranking and inconsistency testing; random-effects models were fitted for four outcomes, whereas a fixed-effect model was used for neuropsychiatric symptoms because the random-effects model was not estimable. Review Manager 5.3 was used for pairwise subgroup analyses and risk-of-bias visualization. Evidence certainty for each network contrast was appraised with CINeMA 2.0.0 using the six standard domains.

Results

Thirty-nine RCTs involving 3,039 participants according to the updated study-characteristics table were included in the final analysis. The network meta-analysis revealed that technology-enhanced interventions (SMD = 1.62, 95% CI: 0.95-2.29) and physical function-oriented interventions (SMD = 1.39, 95% CI: 0.76-2.02) were superior to routine care in improving cognitive function, with Tech ranking first (SUCRA = 91.4%). Physical function-oriented interventions ranked highest for daily living ability (SUCRA = 86.8%), although global network inconsistency was detected (P = 0.0231). For depressive symptoms, technology-enhanced interventions ranked first (SUCRA = 84.1%). Technology-enhanced interventions (MD = 5.63, 95% CI: 0.66-10.60) yielded the greatest relative improvement in quality of life (SUCRA = 86.3%), but the network showed global inconsistency (P = 0.0064). CINeMA appraisals identified low confidence for 18 of 76 contrasts and very low confidence for 58, including all 15 quality-of-life contrasts. Evidence for neuropsychiatric symptoms was exploratory: only four trials contributed to a sparse fixed-effect network, the apparent large indirect effect was dependent on one feasibility trial, and a robust intervention hierarchy could not be established. Subgroup analyses indicated no clear difference between human-centered and environment-integrated interventions for cognition or between cultural backgrounds for daily living ability. In contrast, interventions were associated with improved quality of life among residents with mild cognitive impairment (MD = +3.98, 95% CI: 2.22-5.74; P for subgroup difference = 0.004).

Conclusions

Among five categories of non-pharmacological interventions, technology-enhanced interventions showed the highest relative ranking for cognitive function, depressive symptoms and quality of life, whereas physical function-oriented interventions ranked first for daily living ability. Evidence was insufficient to establish a reliable hierarchy for neuropsychiatric symptoms. However, significant inconsistency for daily living ability and quality of life, changes in cognitive rankings after excluding pilot studies, and the dependence of the neuropsychiatric findings on a single feasibility trial warrant cautious interpretation. The effectiveness of interventions may also vary by cognitive impairment severity, with improved quality of life observed among residents with mild impairment. These results can inform individualized nursing-home care, and CINeMA ratings were low or very low for every contrast; thus the rankings should not be regarded as definitive evidence of superiority.

title: Application of Data Science for COVID-19 Modeling in Africa: A Comparative Study of ARIMA and ANN Models, a Retrospective Time-Series Analysis.
abstract:
Background and aims

The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the urgent need for robust forecasting tools to guide public health responses in Africa, where data infrastructure remains limited, and epidemic dynamics differ substantially from high-income settings.

Methods

Daily COVID-19 surveillance data were obtained from the WHO COVID-19 Dashboard for Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa, and Tunisia. ARIMA models were fitted using the auto.arima function in R, with stationarity assessed using Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) and Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin (KPSS) tests. ANN models were implemented using the nnetar algorithm, configured with lag parameter p = 7, seasonal lag p = 1, hidden layer size of 10 nodes, and 20 repeats. Model accuracy was evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and R-squared (R 2).

Results

ARIMA outperformed ANN for four countries (Egypt, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria), while ANN performed better for three countries (Ghana, Tunisia, South Africa). Egypt achieved the highest forecast accuracy (MAPE = 0.09% for ARIMA). South Africa presented the greatest forecasting challenge due to high volatility and multiple distinct waves, though ANN substantially outperformed ARIMA in this setting, reducing RMSE by 56% and MAPE by 51%. Negative R 2 values for six of seven countries reflected the structural inability of backward-looking autoregressive models to anticipate variant-driven wave peaks, consistent with limitations documented in COVID-19 forecasting literature.

Conclusion

Neither model is universally superior; model selection should be context-dependent. ANN is recommended for settings with stable case fatality rates and complex non-linear dynamics (e.g., Ghana) and for high-volume settings with multiple distinct waves (e.g., South Africa). ARIMA is recommended for moderate-transmission settings with more linear patterns where interpretability is prioritized.

title: 3D non-rigid motion correction using Doppler-regularized optical flow for coronary ultrasound localization microscopy in beating heart.
abstract: Objectives. Coronary microvascular disease, involving vessels smaller than 300µm, contributes significantly to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. However, direct visualization of coronary microcirculation remains challenging because current clinical imaging modalities lack the spatial and temporal resolution required to resolve the microvascular network. Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables imaging beyond the diffraction limit and can reveal coronary microvascular structures but is altered by large motion. This work addresses 3D non-rigid motion in coronary ULM to enable more accurate reconstruction and visualization of the coronary microvascular network.Approach. Here we developed a 3D non-rigid motion correction framework based on optical flow with Doppler velocity regularization to compensate for cardiac motion in 3D ULM of beating rat hearts.Main results. The method was validated in perfusedex vivobeating rat hearts imaged with ultrafast 3D ultrasound. Motion correction enhanced microbubbles tracking density and vessels delineation, enabling visualization of microvessels below 100µm and velocity measurements with spatial resolution of at least 40µm.Significance. This framework advances volumetric assessment of coronary microcirculation, facilitating longer acquisition windows and may support future cardiovascular research and clinical applications by overcoming motion-induced limitations in 3D coronary ULM.

title: Real-time Radiation Exposure Monitoring in the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory Using a Digital RRPD Dosimeter.
abstract: Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation remains an important concern for healthcare professionals working in x-ray-guided interventional environments. Conventional passive dosimetry provides retrospective dose assessment and does not permit immediate modification of operator behavior. We evaluated the feasibility and practical utility of a real-time radiation personal dosimeter (RRPD) during three chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention procedures performed in a cardiac catheterization laboratory. Wearable dosimeters were positioned on the lead aprons of the primary and secondary operators and provided continuous wireless measurements of the dose rate and cumulative radiation exposure. Procedural parameters, including fluoroscopy time, air kerma, dose-area product (DAP), cine acquisition count, and operator dose, were recorded and compared with commonly reported reference ranges for CTO interventions. Radiation exposure increases with procedural complexity. Antegrade CTO procedures demonstrated fluoroscopy time, air kerma, and DAP values below the typical reference ranges, whereas a complex retrograde CTO procedure was associated with higher values consistent with prolonged fluoroscopy. Real-time visualization of radiation peaks was associated with timely operator adjustments without too much clinical interference, including reduced angulation and limitations of cine imaging. The primary operator exposure exceeded the secondary operator exposure in all cases. These findings indicate that real-time personal dosimetry enables continuous exposure monitoring and may support radiation-protective behaviors during high-dose interventional procedures.

title: Population-scale integration of spatial omics networks for clinical prediction and biological discovery by SPIN.
abstract: Spatial omics enables the integration of high-dimensional molecular organization with clinical outcomes, yet incorporating spatial single-cell information into predictive models at the population scale remains challenging. We introduce SPIN (spatial predictive integration network), which integrates subject-specific, cell-type level, spatially informed co-expression or co-abundance networks for population-scale clinical prediction. Current implementation of SPIN includes three key modules: network construction, molecular-to-clinical prediction by Bayesian scalar-on-network regression with manifold learning (BSNMani), and visualization & interpretation module. In the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) transcriptomics cohort, SPIN achieved an accuracy of 0.81 for dementia-status prediction and revealed co-expression subnetworks with clear biological relevance. SPIN also achieved robust survival prediction in a breast cancer single-cell proteomics cohort (C-index = 0.78), identifying two survival-associated spatial proteomic subnetworks. In summary, SPIN is an interpretable tool for spatial-omics-based clinical outcome prediction at the population scale.

title: Robotics in endoscopic spine surgery: a scoping review of clinical applications, workflow integration, and patient outcomes.
abstract: Robotic and endoscopic technologies are increasingly being combined in spine surgery, yet the clinical literature remains fragmented across procedures, platforms, and robotic functions. We conducted a scoping review to map clinical applications of robot-assisted endoscopic spine surgery, describe how robotic systems are incorporated into endoscopic workflows, and summarize the technical, perioperative, and patient-centered outcomes reported to date. PubMed and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Human clinical reports were eligible when endoscopy constituted part of the operative visualization or working approach and a robotic system directly assisted the same spinal procedure. Study selection was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Of 374 records identified, 122 duplicates were removed and 252 records were screened. Sixty-six reports were sought, 13 were not retrieved, 53 full texts were assessed, and 24 studies were included. The evidence comprised 11 comparative studies, four uncontrolled clinical series, and nine case-based or technical clinical reports. Applications ranged from discectomy and decompression to interbody fusion, pars repair, infection, trauma, and thoracic or craniovertebral procedures. Robots were used for trajectory planning, localization, percutaneous access, guidewire or pedicle screw placement, drilling, endoscope stabilization, and interbody instrumentation. Comparative studies most often showed gains in fluoroscopy use, access efficiency, or instrumentation accuracy; patient-reported outcomes were usually similar between groups. Robotic-endoscopic integration is clinically feasible across an expanding range of spinal procedures, but its patient-level value remains incompletely defined.

title: SPARC: Sectorized Partial-Angle Reconstruction Based Motion Correction Method for Multi-Phase CCTA.
abstract:
Objective

Multi-phase Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography (CCTA) provides a clear visualization of coronary arteries, offering comprehensive and reliable imaging support for the clinical diagnosis of coronary artery disease. However, traditional motion correction reconstruction algorithms lack reconstruction robustness despite their interpretability, while deep learning reconstruction methods achieve high imaging quality at the expense of interpretability and anatomical reliability in clinical CCTA practice. This study aims to simultaneously achieve interpretable and robust multi-phase coronary reconstruction. Approach. We propose a motion trajectory estimation and motion correction framework termed sectorized partial-angle reconstruction-based motion correction (SPARC) for CCTA. The proposed framework integrates sectorized partial-angle reconstructions, a spatio-temporal cascaded network for coronary centerline extraction, and a phase-accumulated fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm for motion trajectory estimation. These components work together to minimize motion estimation errors and enhance the quality of motion-corrected reconstruction. Main results. Experimental results from both simulations and clinical studies demonstrate that SPARC achieves superior reconstruction performance compared with existing methods. SPARC effectively reduces coronary motion artifacts and restores clear vessel structures while preserving reconstruction fidelity, achieving the best scores on all metrics. Significance. By preserving both interpretability and anatomical reliability while effectively reducing motion artifacts, SPARC provides a clinically deployable solution for motion-corrected multi-phase CCTA, supporting more reliable imaging for coronary artery disease diagnosis.

title: A pyridyl-benzopyridoindole-dione probe for ultrafast fluorometric selective detection of diethyl chlorophosphate (DCP) nerve agent mimic with latent fingerprint and logic gate applications.
abstract: Organophosphorus nerve agents pose severe threats to public health and national security, driving the urgent need for rapid, sensitive and field-deployable detection system. In the present work, a pyridyl benzopyridoindole dione (PBID) fluorophore featuring naphthoquinone core as an intramolecular charge-transfer (ICT) modulator is reported for selective and sensitive fluorescence "turn-off" detection of diethyl chlorophosphate (DCP). DCP addition caused five-fold emission quenching at 615 nm with a visual orange-to-lavender color change under UV light (365 nm). The response is attributed to pyridine nitrogen phosphorylation followed by hydrolysis to protonated PBID, as supported by 1H NMR titration and DFT calculations. The probe enables ultrafast detection within 15 s, achieving limit of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) values of 0.67 and 2.24 µM, respectively. Beyond solution-phase sensing, PBID was successfully translated into practical platforms, including paper-based test strips, solid-state reversible sensing, latent fingerprint (LFP) visualization on non-porous surfaces and smartphone-integrated RGB colorimetric analysis for on-site quantification. PBID also enabled an "IMPLICATION" molecular logic gate and showed reliable DCP recovery from environmental water and soil samples. An Analytical GREEnness (AGREE) metric score of 0.80 further supports the sustainability of the method.

title: OCCLUDE: Final Results from the Prospective Multicenter Real-World Study.
abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of Obsidio Conformable Embolic for vascular embolization.

Materials and methods

OCCLUDE is a multicenter, prospective, single-arm, real-world clinical registry. Patients (n=125) from 19 centers underwent embolization with Obsidio and were followed for 1 month. The primary effectiveness endpoint was technical success, defined as occlusion of target vessel(s), confirmed by angiography or visualization of an Obsidio cast on fluoroscopy/imaging immediately post-embolization. Clinical success, a secondary endpoint, was defined as absence of target vessel bleeding within 30 days. The primary safety endpoint was freedom from major adverse events (MAEs), defined as non-target embolization meeting serious adverse event criteria, unintended target organ/soft tissue infarction, vessel perforation/injury, or catheter entrapment through 30 days.

Results

Indications included bleeding/hemorrhage (n=98; 78.4%), hypervascular tumor (HVT; n=19; 15.2%), and other (n=8; 6.4%). Median age was 63.0 years; 88.8% (n=111) had a single target embolized. Target arteries were renal (25.5%), non-gastrointestinal (GI) visceral (17.4%), upper GI (9.3%), extremity (3.7%), lower GI (2.5%), and other (41.6%). Among 161 embolized vessels, 38 (23.6%) received another embolic with Obsidio, with 84.2% used before Obsidio. Technical success was 100%. Clinical success was assessed in hemorrhage (n=98) and bleeding HVT (n=7) cases (n=105 total). Clinical success was 100% among 97/105 evaluable patients (0% rebleeding); 8 lacked 30-day follow-up. Freedom from MAEs was 97.4% (113/116), and no catheter entrapment occurred.

Conclusions

OCCLUDE demonstrated real-world safety and effectiveness of Obsidio, achieving 100% technical and clinical success, with a low MAE rate across diverse target vessels.

title: Evaluation of a novel transseptal puncture device for use in cardiac procedures requiring left atrial access.
abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is the first step in percutaneous left-heart interventions including atrial fibrillation ablation, left atrial appendage occlusion, and percutaneous mitral valve repair/replacement. Current TSP techniques remain limited by suboptimal imaging visualization, lack of precise control over puncture sites, and a steep learning curve. The Protaryx transseptal puncture device was designed to address these limitations by incorporating a novel atraumatic highly echogenic deployable and retractable nitinol mesh end effector mounted on an extendable catheter. The key advantages of the Protaryx TSP device are the maneuverability of the extendable catheter and the visibility of the end effector that combine to enable precise targeting of the fossa ovalis during TSP. Here, we provide an overview of challenges with transseptal puncture, an overview of the Protaryx device, and early clinical evidence. This includes results of the 5-patient prospective non-randomized observational first-in-human experience with the Protaryx TSP catheter. This study demonstrated early feasibility and safety, with rapid on-target puncture of the fossa ovalis, zero adverse events, and 100% success of structural heart interventions following TSP. The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of the Protaryx device has increased options for interventional cardiologists and electrophysiologists seeking to streamline left-sided structural heart intervention.

title: A ratiometric dual-modal photoacoustic and near-infrared fluorescence probe for in vivo spatiotemporal mapping of butyrylcholinesterase in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) is a critical biomarker for the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology; however, real-time visualization of its dynamic activity changes in deep biological tissues remains highly challenging. Herein, we report the development of BChE-PA, a novel hemicyanine-based dual-modal probe for the ratiometric detection of BChE through integrated near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence and photoacoustic (PA) imaging. The probe design utilizes a specific cyclopropanecarbonyl recognition moiety that effectively masks the internal charge transfer (ICT) process of the fluorophore. Enzymatic cleavage of the cyclopropanecarbonyl group by BChE restores the ICT effect and extends the molecular π-conjugation, triggering a significant 93 nm bathochromic shift in absorption (from 622 nm to 715 nm) and a dramatic NIR fluorescence "turn-on" response. BChE-PA exhibits an exceptional detection limit of 0.03 U/mL and high selectivity over competing esterases. By leveraging the ratiometric PA signal (PA<sub>755</sub>/PA<sub>680</sub>), we successfully performed self-calibrating, deep-tissue mapping of elevated BChE levels in the brains of APP/PS1 transgenic mice. This dual-modal platform provides a robust tool for the spatiotemporal tracking of BChE, bridging the gap between molecular environmental surveillance and clinical neuroimaging.

title: Far Medial Endoscopic Transcervical Approach for Excision of a Recurrent Clival Chordoma Involving the Parapharyngeal and Prevertebral Spaces.
abstract:
Background and importance

Chordoma is a rare, malignant neoplasm arising from notochordal remnants. Addressing recurrent disease is challenging due to scar tissue formation, proximity to neurovascular structures, and altered clinical anatomy from prior surgery and/or radiation therapy. Herein, this work describes technical considerations and operative principles utilized in endoscopic transcervical resection for recurrent craniocervical chordoma extending into the right prevertebral/parapharyngeal space.

Clinical presentation

A 16-year-old male with a history of clival chordoma was found to have an expansile mass spanning the C1-C2 levels in the right prevertebral/parapharyngeal space on surveillance MRI. He had previously undergone definitive chemoradiation therapy as this tumor was initially misdiagnosed as rhabdomyosarcoma in another country at 13 years of age. He subsequently underwent multiple surgical procedures and treatments, including far lateral craniotomy with occiput-to-C2 posterior spinal fusion, combined endoscopic endonasal and transoral resection, and definitive proton therapy at our institution. An endoscopic transcervical approach was selected for salvage surgery as this provided an unoperated corridor with direct access to the neoplastic focus. The patient underwent uncomplicated gross total resection of recurrent chordoma.

Conclusion

This case demonstrates the safety and efficacy of far medial endoscopic neck dissection for recurrent craniocervical chordoma extending into parapharyngeal/retropharyngeal space in a pediatric patient. Key advantages of this approach include early identification and control of proximal great vessels and lower cranial nerves, dynamic visualization, bimanual surgical technique, and low risk of suboptimal wound healing by avoiding previously operated and/or irradiated tissue.

title: Safety, procedural completion and feasibility of unsedated gastroscopy in a large patient cohort.
abstract:
Background and study aims

Sedation is commonly used during esophagogastroduodenoscopy to improve patient comfort; however, it may increase risks and costs. This study aimed to evaluate the safety, procedural completion, and feasibility of unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy in a large patient cohort.

Patients and methods

This retrospective study included 1245 patients who underwent unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy between September 2015 and June 2025. Demographic and clinical characteristics, including age, gender, indication for endoscopy, and whether the procedure was completed, were analyzed. Procedural completion was defined as the successful completion of the procedure with adequate visualization of the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum. Procedure duration and endoscopic findings were also evaluated. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 21.0, with a significance level of p < 0.05.

Results

Of the 1245 patients, 519 (41.7%) were male and 726 (58.3%) were female, with a mean age of 49.03 ± 14.27 years. The most common indication for endoscopy was dyspepsia (55.3%). The procedure was successfully completed in 1196 patients (96.1%), while 49 patients (3.9%) were unable to complete the procedure. The mean procedure time was 4.99 ± 1.45 min. Procedural completion rates were not significantly associated with gender or age (p = 0.250 and p = 0.190, respectively), but were significantly higher among patients with prior gastroscopy experience (p = 0.029). No major complications occurred.

Conclusion

Unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy is a safe, feasible diagnostic method with a high procedural completion rate in appropriately selected patients. Proper patient education and prior endoscopic experience significantly improve procedural completion. This approach avoids the risks associated with sedation and may provide a lower procedural cost than sedated endoscopy in routine clinical practice.

title: Deep Learning-Accelerated 3D T2 CUBE MRI of the Cochlea at 1.5T and 3T: Sonic DL With AIR Recon DL Versus AIR Recon DL Alone.
abstract:
Background and purpose

Three-dimensional fast spin-echo MR cisternography (CUBE) of the internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) requires longer acquisition times that can limit clinical throughput. We evaluated whether a deep learning (DL)-based highly accelerated reconstruction technique, Sonic DL`™ (SDL), combined with a commercially available DL denoising reconstruction (AIR™ Recon DL, ARDL), preserves or improves subjective image quality and cochlear anatomy visualization relative to standard CUBE-ARDL while shortening scan time.

Materials and methods

Consecutive patients underwent brain MRI for suspected IAC pathology at 1.5T and 3T with paired acquisition of standard 3D CUBE-ARDL and an accelerated 3D CUBE-SDL sequence. Both used the same voxel size at 1.5T (0.6x0.6x1.2 mm3) and 3T (0.6x0.6x0.6 mm3). Scan times for CUBE-ARDL versus CUBE-SDL were 2:33 versus 1:41 min at 1.5T and 1:55 versus 1:11 min at 3T. Two independent neuroradiologists blinded to MRI acquisition method scored randomized, de-identified images on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains (overall image quality, noise, sharpness, artifacts, cochlear anatomy visualization). Reader-averaged scores for CUBE-ARDL and CUBE-SDL were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with reader-specific and cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) sensitivity analyses and false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) quantified inter-reader reliability for each technique; Gwet's AC2 and weighted (Conger's) kappa with linear ordinal weights quantified pooled inter-reader agreement.

Results

After exclusion of 5 training cases per field strength, 49 (1.5T) and 34 (3T) patients were analyzed. CUBE-SDL scored significantly better than CUBE-ARDL for all five domains at both field strengths (all FDR-adjusted P < .001), consistently for each reader and in the CLMM. Inter-reader reliability (ICC) for CUBE-SDL was moderate-to-excellent at 3T (0.63-0.92) and moderate at 1.5T (0.65-0.74), generally exceeding CUBE-ARDL (3T: 0.35-0.61; 1.5T: 0.50-0.71). Pooled inter-reader agreement (Gwet's AC2) ranged from 0.56 to 0.89.

Conclusions

A combined Sonic DL acceleration with ARDL-denoised reconstruction for 3D T2 CUBE produced significantly higher subjective image quality at both 1.5T and 3T, and, at 3T, higher inter-reader reliability than standard CUBE-ARDL, while shortening acquisition time by 34%-38%. These findings support further evaluation, including diagnostic accuracy studies, of CUBE-SDL as an alternative to CUBE-ARDL.

title: Recent advances in photoacoustic imaging for breast reconstruction using the abdominal flap.
abstract: Recent advances in diagnostic imaging have significantly impacted surgical planning and options. In breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps, a method employing flaps from the lower abdomen allows for a high-quality reconstruction with a morphology and texture resembling those of the contralateral breast. Understanding microvascular patterns is crucial in this surgery to prevent volume deficiencies and contribute to successful tissue transplantation while maintaining the softness of the tissue. While the location and number of "perforators"-arteriovenous bundles penetrating the anterior sheath of the rectus abdominis-have traditionally been the focus, recent studies have further emphasized the importance of selecting appropriate perforating vessels to maintain the vascular network within the superficial adipose tissue and subcutaneous tissue and to elevate a high-quality flap with extensive and stable blood flow. Clinical studies using contrast-enhanced CT have drawn attention to the midline-crossing arterial network, demonstrating its relationship with a wide range of hemodynamic areas. Preoperatively, clearly identifying the blood vessels linking the left and right sides of the abdominal midline provides valuable information for planning free DIEP flaps for breast reconstruction, ensuring stable blood flow to the flap. However, clear visualization with contrast-enhanced CT requires high volumes of contrast agents, and color Doppler ultrasound has difficulty visualizing horizontally; therefore, a non-invasive and superior imaging method is required. Photoacoustic imaging can comprehensively and noninvasively visualize the subcutaneous vascular network and is attracting attention as a new preoperative examination technique. We conducted clinical research using newly developed medical photoacoustic imaging and reported the results and future challenges in several publications. We have also recently reported the impact of abdominal surgical scars on the midline-crossing artery. This review summarizes the current trends in preoperative vascular studies for breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps and discusses the current state of evolving photoacoustic imaging technology.

title: Navigated robotic guidance for minimally invasive bertolotti resection technical feasibility and workflow evaluation.
abstract: Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This original article evaluates the technical feasibility and workflow of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow to perform minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A technical framework is presented for preoperative computerized computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, and navigated robotic trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of the planned navigated robotic steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but they should not be interpreted as proof of superior outcomes. This initial paper outlines a novel technique, however; further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance can be established.

title: Bibliometric analysis of nanotechnology research in acute kidney injury and emerging trends.
abstract:
Aim

This study aimed to systematically characterize the global research landscape, knowledge structure, and thematic evolution of nanotechnology research in acute kidney injury (AKI) using bibliometric and visualization approaches.

Materials & methods

Publications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for the period up to December 31, 2025. After eligibility and relevance screening, 705 publications were included. CiteSpace, VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, and GraphPad Prism were used to analyze publication trends, contributions of countries, institutions, authors, and journals, collaboration and co-citation networks, highly cited references, and keyword patterns.

Results

Publication output increased substantially over the study period, particularly in recent years. China contributed the largest number of publications, followed by the United States, while institutional output was concentrated predominantly in China. Collaboration networks demonstrated extensive but uneven connections across countries and institutions. Journal of Controlled Release was the most productive journal, whereas Kidney International was the most highly co-cited journal. The most frequent keywords were "acute kidney injury," "nanoparticles," and "oxidative stress." Temporal analyses showed a gradual evolution from broad experimental and imaging-related applications toward greater emphasis on oxidative stress, reactive oxygen species, therapeutic delivery, and mechanism-oriented nanotechnology. Ferroptosis also appeared among the more recent trend topics.

Conclusion

Nanotechnology research in AKI has expanded into an increasingly interdisciplinary field integrating nephrology, materials science, nanomedicine, and drug-delivery research. Current themes emphasize oxidative injury, targeted delivery, and increasingly mechanism-oriented nanoplatforms. Future research should prioritize rigorous evaluation of targeting performance, pharmacokinetics, biosafety, reproducibility, and translational feasibility to determine the clinical value of emerging nanotechnology strategies for AKI.

title: The effect of magnetic resonance image slice thickness and voxel geometry on digital dental implant planning: an in vitro study.
abstract:
Objectives

To evaluate the effect of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) slice thickness and voxel geometry on digital dental implant planning compared to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).

Methods

Edentulous phantoms were scanned using CBCT and two MRI protocols: anisotropic and isotropic. Two calibrated examiners digitally planned the position of four implants for each sample (n = 8) per exam (CBCT, anisotropic and isotropic). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using implant angular deviation and linear measurements. Image quality was evaluated using a questionnaire regarding visualization of anatomical structures. Cost-to-planning-time ratio was assessed by exam costs per minute of planning. The Friedman and Wilcoxon tests were used to evaluate differences in diagnostic accuracy, planning time, and cost-to-planning-time ratio. Image quality ratings on a 5-point scale were classified as non-valid (≤ 2) or valid (≥ 3) for clinical use. Reliability was assessed by percentage agreement, and differences were evaluated using the chi-square test.

Results

A total of 96 implants were planned, with 32 in each exam. No significant differences were observed between exams for angular deviation (p > 0.197), linear measurements (p > 0.305), image quality (p > 0.132), or planning time (p = 0.093). However, CBCT had lower cost-to-planning-time ratio than anisotropic and isotropic MRI (p = 0.012), which did not differ from each other (p = 1.000). Inter-examiner agreement on image quality for anisotropic and isotropic MRI varied widely, with lower ratings for the mandibular nerve canal.

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected among the imaging protocols in diagnostic accuracy or image quality under the investigated in vitro conditions.

title: Responsive accumulation of ultrasmall DNA@WO<sub>3-<i>x</i></sub> nanodots for suppressing tumor progression and metastasis <i>via</i> single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects.
abstract: Effective treatment for malignant tumors continues to represent an urgent unmet clinical need. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) constitutes a therapeutic challenge on account of its aggressive nature and limited response to conventional therapies. Radiotherapy serves as a cornerstone for cervical cancer treatment. Nevertheless, radioresistance frequently gives rise to therapeutic failure in cervical cancer. We developed ultrasmall, pH-responsive DNA@WO3-x nanodots to enhance the accumulation of nanodots within tumors, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy. The nanodots undergo intelligent self-assembly within the acidic tumor microenvironment, leading to enhanced accumulation and retention. DNA@WO3-x functions dually as an effective computed tomography (CT) contrast agent for tumor visualization and a potent radiosensitizer. The high-Z element tungsten and remarkable photothermal conversion capability in the NIR-II window enable synergistic radio-photothermal therapy (RT-PTT). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the combined treatment via single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects potently suppresses the growth of tumor cells. Consequently, this synergistic strategy achieved remarkable inhibition of primary tumor growth and suppression of distant metastasis in orthotopic TNBC models, with no significant systemic toxicity observed. Furthermore, in vitro validation experiments verified that the developed nanodots can effectively sensitize cervical cancer cells to radiotherapy, thereby achieving prominent anti-tumor therapeutic effects. This work presents a versatile and integrated theranostic strategy that realizes potent tumor suppression via single-nanodot triple-therapeutic effects, offering a promising approach for the precise and effective treatment of aggressive solid tumors.
