title: Development, Validation, and Implementation of a Geography-Specific Syndromic Coding and Reporting System for Snakebite Envenoming (D-SERPENT): Protocol for an Implementation-Effectiveness Hybrid Study.
abstract:
Background

Snakebite envenoming (SBE) is a neglected tropical disease with substantial morbidity and mortality. India accounts for nearly 50% of global snakebite deaths, yet the disease remains underreported due to a lack of standardized documentation and phenotypic classification. Current diagnosis is syndromic and lacks uniform data capture protocols.

Objective

This study aims to develop, validate, and implement a geography-specific syndromic coding and reporting system for SBE to improve standardized documentation, clinical management, surveillance, and epidemiological data quality in selected districts of India.

Methods

This implementation-effectiveness hybrid study will be conducted across 4 study districts in India, representing 4 geographical zones. Retrospective and prospective data will be encoded using a standardized, geography-specific coding system modeled on the International Classification of Diseases and SNOMED Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT). Stakeholders, including clinicians, researchers, and public health specialists, will contribute to the development of the coding system using the Delphi methodology. Training will be provided to project assistants for real-time data entry. A snakebite surveillance dashboard will be developed and hosted by the Indian Council of Medical Research.

Results

The study is expected to establish a standardized, geography-specific syndromic coding and reporting system for SBE across selected districts in India. Its implementation is anticipated to improve classification accuracy, reporting completeness, and epidemiological data quality, thereby strengthening surveillance and supporting evidence-based clinical management and policy planning. The project's funding was approved in January 2025, and participating institutions provided ethics approval between March 2025 and May 2025. The geography-specific syndromic coding framework development, including stakeholder consultations and Delphi rounds, was conducted between June 2025 and August 2025, with prospective implementation of the coding and reporting system planned from September 2025 to September 2026. Data cleaning, validation, and statistical analyses are expected to be completed by March 2027, with the dissemination of findings anticipated in June 2027.

Conclusions

The study proposes a first-of-its-kind phenotypic data-driven approach to snakebite surveillance and treatment in India. The resulting coding system and dashboard will strengthen national reporting and guide future health policy and intervention programs.

title: Development and implementation of an objective framework for measuring clinician faculty research contributions in a Canadian anesthesiology department.
abstract:
Purpose

Given the fiduciary responsibility of an academic clinical department to ensure appropriate use of funds to support research, the Department of Anesthesia, Pain Management and Perioperative Medicine at Dalhousie University (Halifax, NS, Canada) aimed to create a framework to support the allocation of remunerated protected research time to clinician faculty members within the department.

Methods

A departmental Research Accountability Project (RAP) was undertaken in the context of a quality improvement initiative. The RAP initially engaged clinician faculty members in the form of a survey, interviews, and a questionnaire to provide feedback regarding current practices for evaluating protected time for research. On the basis of this feedback, a working group created a list of 151 research outputs encompassing the breadth of research-related activities and assigned scores based on their relative merit. Clinicians with protected research time completed their academic profile, and individual point allocations were calculated. Scores were then weighted by different categories (e.g., publications, grant capture, presentations), and a RAP dashboard was developed to capture research outputs, assign scores, and generate a reporting/feedback mechanism for further analysis.

Results

Faculty members acknowledged the importance of clinicians having remunerated protected time to carry out research; nevertheless, there was scepticism with respect to how protected research time was managed. These data were then assessed by the working group, and using the RAP metric, individual researcher reports consisting of scores and recommendations were sent to the department head for final evaluation. These reports formed the basis of the researchers' annual academic performance review and consideration for continuance.

Conclusions

The RAP scoring system provides an objective measure of remunerated protected research time for clinicians to assist in researcher accountability.

title: Adverse reactions associated with henna-based cosmetic products: a twenty-two-year pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA adverse event reporting system.
abstract:
Background

Henna-based cosmetic products, particularly those adulterated with para-phenylenediamine (PPD), are an increasingly recognized cause of adverse skin reactions. Despite widespread consumer use, population-level pharmacovigilance data from US regulatory sources remain limited.

Objective

To characterize the clinical, demographic, and temporal patterns of henna-associated adverse events reported to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and to identify factors associated with case seriousness.

Methods

Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of henna-related adverse event reports extracted from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System Cosmetic Public Dashboard, excluding products unrelated to henna (Lawsonia inermis) such as Jagua-based formulations. Statistical analyses included chi-square, Spearman's rank correlation, and Proportional Reporting Ratio disproportionality analysis.

Results

A total of 110 cases were identified (female: 65.5%; pediatric cases <18 years). Black Henna products (classified by product name) represented the largest product category (n = 47, 42.7%). The most frequently reported reactions were pruritus (39.3%), hypersensitivity (32.1%). Serious cases 50.0% of the dataset. No statistically significant association was found between gender and seriousness (χ2=0.133, p = 0.715). hypersensitivity (PRR = 1.54, 95% CI: 0.81-2.92, χ2=1.74, p = 0.187) and urticaria (PRR = 2.26, 95% CI: 0.82-6.18, χ2=2.51, p = 0.113) showed elevated PRR values; however, neither met the predefined signal threshold (PRR ≥ 2.0, χ2≥4.0, n ≥ 3), and no formal disproportionality signal was identified.

Conclusions

Henna-associated adverse events affect predominantly young females and pediatric patients. These findings support enhanced regulatory scrutiny under the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA), mandatory product labeling, and targeted consumer safety communication.

title: Developing a digital knowledge-to-practice framework for urinary device management and CAUTI surveillance.
abstract:
Background

Inappropriate urinary device use and catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) contribute to preventable patient harm, antimicrobial resistance, incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD) and prolonged hospitalisation.

Aim

To describe the development, implementation and evaluation of a digitally enabled urinary device knowledge-to-practice framework designed to strengthen clinical governance, improve CAUTI surveillance and support harm prevention.

Methods

A practice-based implementation programme was led by the Continence Lead Nurse at University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust. Following an evidence review, the Continence Lead Nurse independently undertook a prospective clinical audit of CAUTI symptoms and microbiology findings. The audit informed the decision to embed CAUTI symptom prompts within electronic catheter care plans and develop CAUTIon+, a digital surveillance dashboard. Evidence-based urinary device pathways and digital care plans were integrated into trust-wide clinical policy. A female external catheter (FEC) pathway was evaluated through a 6-week feasibility study and a separate 6-month value-based procurement evaluation.

Results

Implementation established daily prospective CAUTI surveillance through CAUTIon+, supporting earlier identification of suspected infection and structured clinical review. In the initial FEC evaluation, all nine patients reported positive experiences, while 19 of 21 staff respondents highly recommended the device. The subsequent procurement evaluation recorded a 93% reduction in IAD cases (43 to 3), with an estimated 132 bed days avoided and £67 896.30 in reported net savings.

Conclusion

Integrating digital urinary device care plans, trust-wide clinical policy and CAUTIon+ surveillance translated evidence into routine practice and strengthened urinary device stewardship. The framework supports earlier clinical intervention and antimicrobial stewardship, with the potential to contribute to prevention of urinary-source sepsis. It aligns with the NHS 10-year health plan's shift towards digital, preventive health care and offers a model for wider NHS evaluation.

title: Design of a Multifaceted Transitional Care Digital Intervention: Double Diamond Approach.
abstract:
Background

Transitions of care, where patients move between clinical settings or providers, pose considerable risks to patient safety, situations exacerbated by the absence of adequate digital infrastructure that enables information exchange. The timeliness and accuracy of medication information transfer are central to ensuring patient safety during transitions of care, including post-discharge from the hospital. In designing a multifaceted digital intervention to support the transfer of medication information from hospital to community settings, it was necessary to gauge the views of all relevant stakeholders on the practical challenges involved in transferring medication information.

Objective

This study aimed to define the challenges experienced by stakeholders, develop potential solutions, and use a collaborative approach to design a multifaceted digital intervention that spans hospital and community settings.

Methods

This project involved multiple health service organizations in Queensland, Australia's second-largest state geographically. Design of the intervention was guided by the United Kingdom Design Council's Double Diamond Framework. This phased approach is particularly suitable for complex interventions involving multiple stakeholders. Over 12 months, we held an initial workshop with consumers (n=4), hospital clinicians (n=6), and primary care clinicians (n=7), and then convened over 50 hours of committee meetings, working groups, and consultations, undertook a system-walkthrough, and assessed the feasibility of the intervention. Participants were patients with relevant lived experience, clinicians, and those with technical, clinical governance, policy, research, and digital health implementation expertise.

Results

Challenges described by workshop participants included fragmented digital systems across care settings, delays in discharge documentation reaching primary care clinicians, and current systems that function as incomplete or inconsistently used sources of medication information. Based on stakeholder consultation, our multifaceted intervention comprises both clinician- and patient-facing elements. These include a hospital-based Pharmacist Navigator role to facilitate post-discharge handover; a clinical dashboard for identifying and stratifying patient risk of medication misadventure; a software application for post-discharge pharmacist-led medication review and communication of the review to the patient's general practitioner (GP); a Pharmacist Navigator notifying GPs of a patient's hospital stay; patient education materials; and online training for community pharmacists conducting the medication reviews.

Conclusions

Designing a multifaceted digital intervention to support medication information transfer at hospital discharge required significant time, effort, coordination, and engagement from a large number of stakeholders with various roles and areas of expertise. Key learnings are that transitional care interventions must be flexible and adaptable to align with the complex, evolving nature of health care, and that the success of a digital intervention relies heavily on human engagement and ongoing support.
